fact: The Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education's EMIS Report, cited by NewZimbabwe, shows 39,736 learners dropped out in 2025 (13,032 primary, 26,704 secondary), so the ministry publishes national education statistics through its EMIS.

Kuyenda Collective says Zimbabwe has adopted an EMIS that is used to collect, store and manage education data including enrolment, teacher numbers and educational facilities, though most rural schools lack access to feed it in real time.

The Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education says it submits school enrolment figures compiled through the revised EMIS to the Ministry of Finance for annual education budgets, and 12,324 schools nationwide have been equipped to use it (GPE blog by UNICEF Zimbabwe).

The article cites 2024 data and national figures from the official Zimbabwe Education Management Information System (EMIS) Report, such as 68 percent of schools lacking internet and pupil-to-computer ratios of 1:68 and 1:27.
